mishnayot.he: שְׁלשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְאֶחָד, חַיָּבִין לְזַמֵּן. אָכַל דְּמַאי, וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ, וְהַשַּׁמָּשׁ שֶׁאָכַל כַּזַּיִת, וְהַכּוּתִי, מְזַמְּנִין עֲלֵיהֶם. אֲבָל אָכַל טֶבֶל, וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ, וְהַשַּׁמָּשׁ שֶׁאָכַל פָּחוֹת מִכַּזַּיִת, וְהַנָּכְרִי, אֵין מְזַמְּנִין עֲלֵיהֶם:
mishnayot.en: This mishna sets out the essential halakhot pertaining to the invitation to recite Grace after Meals after a joint meal [zimmun]: Three people who ate as one are required to form a zimmun and recite Grace after Meals. If, among the diners, one ate doubtfully tithed produce [demai], and first tithe from which its teruma was already taken, or second tithe, and consecrated food that were redeemed and therefore permitted to be eaten; and even the waiter who served the meal to the diners and who ate at least an olive-bulk from the meal, and the Samaritan [Kuti] who ate with two others at a meal; each of these people is included among the three to obligate those with whom they ate in a zimmun. However, one who ate untithed produce [tevel], and first tithe from which its teruma was not separated, and second tithe, and consecrated food that were not redeemed, and the waiter who did not eat an olive-bulk, and the gentile who ate with two Jews, none of these people is included among the three to obligate those with whom they ate in a zimmun.

mishnayot.he: נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים, אֵין מְזַמְּנִין עֲלֵיהֶם. עַד כַּמָּה מְזַמְּנִין, עַד כַּזָּיִת. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, עַד כַּבֵּיצָה:
mishnayot.en: Women, slaves, and minors do not obligate those with whom they ate in a zimmun. How much must one eat to obligate those with whom he ate in a zimmun? An olive-bulk of food suffices to obligate those with whom they ate in a zimmun. Rabbi Yehuda says: An egg-bulk is the minimum measure to obligate those with whom they ate in a zimmun.

mishnayot.he: כֵּיצַד מְזַמְּנִין, בִּשְׁלשָׁה אוֹמֵר נְבָרֵךְ. בִּשְׁלשָׁה וְהוּא, אוֹמֵר בָּרְכוּ. בַּעֲשָׂרָה, אוֹמֵר נְבָרֵךְ לֵאלֹהֵינוּ. בַּעֲשָׂרָה וָהוּא, אוֹמֵר בָּרְכוּ. אֶחָד עֲשָׂרָה וְאֶחָד עֲשָׂרָה רִבּוֹא. בְּמֵאָה אוֹמֵר, נְבָרֵךְ לַייָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ. בְּמֵאָה וְהוּא, אוֹמֵר בָּרְכוּ. בְּאֶלֶף, אוֹמֵר נְבָרֵךְ לַייָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל. בְּאֶלֶף וְהוּא, אוֹמֵר בָּרְכוּ. בְּרִבּוֹא, אוֹמֵר, נְבָרֵךְ לַייָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֱלֹהֵי הַצְּבָאוֹת יוֹשֵׁב הַכְּרוּבִים עַל הַמָּזוֹן שֶׁאָכָלְנוּ. בְּרִבּוֹא וְהוּא, אוֹמֵר בָּרְכוּ. כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁהוּא מְבָרֵךְ, כָּךְ עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו, בָּרוּךְ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֱלֹהֵי הַצְּבָאוֹת יוֹשֵׁב הַכְּרוּבִים עַל הַמָּזוֹן שֶׁאָכָלְנוּ. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר, לְפִי רֹב הַקָּהָל הֵן מְבָרְכִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמַקְהֵלוֹת בָּרְכוּ אֱלֹהִים, יְיָ מִמְּקוֹר יִשְׂרָאֵל (תהלים סח). אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, מַה מָּצִינוּ בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת, אֶחָד מְרֻבִּין וְאֶחָד מֻעָטִין אוֹמֵר, בָּרְכוּ אֶת יְיָ. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, בָּרְכוּ אֶת יְיָ הַמְבֹרָךְ:
mishnayot.en: The mishna delineates distinctions in the halakhot of the zimmun blessing, based on the number of people present. How does one recite the zimmun? In a group of three people, the one reciting the zimmun says: Let us bless the One from Whose food we have eaten. In a group of three people and him, the one reciting the zimmun says: Bless the One from Whose food we have eaten, as even without him there are enough people to recite the zimmun. With the increase in the number of participants, the blessing is more complex. In a group of ten people, the one reciting the zimmun says: Let us bless our God. In a group of ten people and him, the one reciting the zimmun says: Bless our God. This formula is recited both in a group of ten and in a group of one hundred thousand. In a group of one hundred people, the one reciting the zimmun says: Let us bless the Lord our God. In a group of one hundred people and him, the one reciting the zimmun says: Bless the Lord our God. In a group of one thousand people, the one reciting the zimmun says: Let us bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel. In a group of one thousand people and him, he says: Bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel. In a group of ten thousand people, the one reciting the zimmun says: Let us bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs, for the food that we have eaten. In a group of ten thousand people and him, the one reciting the zimmun says: Bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs, for the food that we have eaten. The principle is that just as he recites the blessing, so too those present recite in response: Blessed be the Lord our God, the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs, for the food that we have eaten. On a similar note, Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: According to the size of the crowd, they recite the blessing, as it is stated: “Bless you God in full assemblies, even the Lord, you who are from the fountain of Israel” (Psalms 68:27). Rabbi Akiva said that there are no distinctions based on the size of the crowd: What do we find in the synagogue? Both when there are many and when there are few, as long as there is a quorum of ten, the prayer leader says: Bless [barekhu] the Lord. Rabbi Yishmael said that in the synagogue, one recites: Bless the Lord the blessed One.

mishnayot.he: שְׁלשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְאֶחָד, אֵינָן רַשָּׁאִין לֵחָלֵק, וְכֵן אַרְבָּעָה, וְכֵן חֲמִשָּׁה. שִׁשָּׁה נֶחֱלָקִין, עַד עֲשָׂרָה. וַעֲשָׂרָה אֵינָן נֶחֱלָקִין, עַד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ עֶשְׂרִים:
mishnayot.en: Three people who ate as one are not permitted to divide and recite Grace after Meals individually; rather, they recite the zimmun together. And the same is true of four who ate together, and the same is true of five. However, a group of six, up to but not including ten people who ate as one, may divide into two groups, each reciting its own zimmun. And a group of ten may not divide into two groups until there are twenty people present. The general principle is that a group may not divide unless the smaller groups will be able to recite the same zimmun formula that the whole group would have recited.

mishnayot.he: שְׁתֵּי חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלוֹת בְּבַיִת אֶחָד, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמִּקְצָתָן רוֹאִין אֵלּוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִצְטָרְפִים לְזִמּוּן. וְאִם לָאו, אֵלּוּ מְזַמְּנִין לְעַצְמָן, וְאֵלּוּ מְזַמְּנִין לְעַצְמָן. אֵין מְבָרְכִין עַל הַיַּיִן עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מְבָרְכִין:
mishnayot.en: The mishna states a halakha with regard to two groups joining together: Two groups that were eating in one house, when some members of each group can see each other, they may combine to form a zimmun. And if not, these recite a zimmun for themselves and those recite a zimmun for themselves. The mishna also speaks of the blessing over wine: One does not recite a blessing over wine until he adds water to it, that is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer. Undiluted wine is too strong to drink and a blessing is inappropriate. And the Rabbis say: Since it is possible to drink undiluted wine, one recites a blessing over it.

english.summary:
Mishnah 1 lists who counts toward the three that obligate a zimmun: someone who ate demai, tithed first tithe, redeemed second tithe or hekdesh, a waiter who ate an olive-bulk, or a Kuti; but not tevel, unredeemed tithes, a waiter who ate less than an olive-bulk, or a gentile.
Mishnah 2 excludes women, slaves and minors, and sets the amount that obligates at an olive-bulk, while Rabbi Yehuda says an egg-bulk.
Mishnah 3 gives the formulas of the zimmun by size of group, from three up to ten thousand, with the opinions of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yishmael.
Mishnah 4 teaches that three, four or five may not divide; six may; ten may not until there are twenty.
Mishnah 5 rules that two groups in one house join if some of them see each other, and records Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages on blessing over undiluted wine.

topics.explanation: Zimmun is the invitation before Grace after Meals, made when three or more eat together. One person says 'let us bless', and the others answer. A group of three is obligated, so the invitation is a duty and not only a custom.

source.name: Bartenura
source.quote: להזדמן יחד לברך בלשון רבים נברך שאכלנו

topics.explanation: Demai is produce of an am ha'aretz, about which it is doubtful whether the tithes were taken. The Rabbis forbade eating it untithed, but the mishnah says a diner who ate it still counts toward the zimmun.

The Kutim were the people brought to the cities of Shomron by the king of Ashur. The mishnah counts the Kuti among those who join a zimmun, because they first adopted the Torah and were careful in the mitzvot they kept.

The mishnah sets a minimum amount for the one who obligates others in a zimmun. The first view is an olive-bulk, and Rabbi Yehuda says an egg-bulk. The Gemara bases the olive-bulk on the verse 'and you shall eat'.

source.name: Tosafot Yom Tov
source.ref: Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Berakhot 7:2:3
source.quote: אכלת זו אכילה ושבעת זו שתיה ואכילה בכזית.

topics.explanation: The mishnah gives the opening of the zimmun by group size: 'let us bless' for three, with the addition of 'our God' for ten, and longer formulas for larger crowds. When the one who invites is not counted among them, he says 'bless'.

source.name: Rambam
source.quote: שמשלשה ועד עשרה אחד מהן מברך נברך שאכלנו

topics.explanation: Three, four or five who ate together may not split into separate zimmunim, because the obligation has already fallen on them. Six may split into two groups of three, but ten may not until there are twenty.

source.name: Bartenura
source.quote: ששה נחלקים. כדי זמון לכאן וכדי זמון לכאן, עד

topics.term: Two groups and a shared waiter
topics.explanation: Two groups in the same house join in a zimmun if some of them can see each other. If not, each group blesses by itself, unless one waiter serves both groups.

source.name: Rambam
source.quote: אבל אם היה להם שמש אחד ואע"פ שלא יראו אלו

topics.explanation: In the time of the mishnah, wine was strong and was drunk after being diluted. Rabbi Eliezer says one does not bless over wine until water is added, while the Sages say one may bless over it.

source.name: Rambam
source.quote: היין של זמן ההוא היה חזק מאד ולא

questions.title: Is eating demai a mitzvah that comes through a transgression?
questions.question: The mishnah lets someone who ate demai count toward a zimmun. Demai is produce of an am ha'aretz from which tithes may not have been separated, and the Rabbis forbade eating it untithed. Why is Grace after Meals on it not a mitzvah that comes through a transgression?

answers.text: Bartenura: most amei ha'aretz do tithe, so there is no mitzvah that comes through a transgression.

sources.name: Bartenura
sources.quote: לא הוי מצוה הבאה בעברה, דרב עמי הארץ מעשרים

answers.text: Tosafot Yom Tov: the owner could declare the produce ownerless and it would then be fit for the poor, so it is not eating in transgression.

sources.name: Tosafot Yom Tov
sources.ref: Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Berakhot 7:1:2
sources.quote: לא הוי אכילה בעבירה דמגו דאי בעי מפקיר לנכסיה

answers.text: Tiferet Yisrael (Yachin): the poor may be fed demai, and the person may also say Grace himself; the mishnah's novelty is that he joins to make a zimmun.

sources.name: Yachin
sources.quote: קמ"ל דאין הבהמ"ז מצוה הבאה בעבירה. מדחזי לעני ומגו

questions.why: It sets the boundary between food that blocks a bracha and food that only carries a rabbinic caution.

questions.title: Why does the mishnah need to teach that the waiter joins the zimmun?
questions.question: Why was it necessary to say that a waiter who ate an olive-bulk obligates the others in a zimmun? What is new in it?

asked_by.name: Melekhet Shelomoh
asked_by.quote: אמאי אצטריך למתני שהשמש מצטרף אלא

answers.text: Melekhet Shelomoh, citing Rabbenu Yonah: others join only if they sat down together, but the waiter joins even though he is not seated as a fixed member.

sources.name: Melekhet Shelomoh
sources.quote: אלא ודאי בא להשמיענו שאע"פ ששאר בנ"א אינם מצטרפין אלא

answers.text: Bartenura: one might think that since the waiter has no fixed place and comes and goes, we do not make a zimmun on him; the mishnah teaches that we do.

sources.name: Bartenura
sources.quote: דמהו דתימא כיון שהשמש אין לו קביעות אלא

questions.why: It shows whether a zimmun depends on sitting together as a fixed group.

questions.title: Does forbidden food block only the zimmun, or the bracha itself?
questions.question: The mishnah says that after eating tevel or unredeemed ma'aser sheni we do not make a zimmun on the diner. Does the diner still bless for himself, or is the bracha itself withheld?

asked_by.name: Tosafot Yom Tov
asked_by.ref: Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Berakhot 7:1:8
asked_by.quote: איכא מרבוותא דסברי דווקא נקט מזמנין.

answers.text: Tosafot Yom Tov: some authorities say the mishnah means only the zimmun, and he still blesses, while others say he does not bless at all.

sources.name: Tosafot Yom Tov
sources.ref: Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Berakhot 7:1:8
sources.quote: איכא מרבוותא דסברי דאף ברכת הנהנין אין

answers.text: Tiferet Yisrael (Yachin): by Ra'avad and Rosh, one who ate by mistake or under duress is not counted for a zimmun but does bless before and after.

sources.name: Yachin
sources.quote: אנן קיי"ל כראב"ד ורא"ש. דבשוגג ואונס. אין מזמנים עליו. דלא

questions.why: It separates the rule of zimmun from the personal obligation to bless.

questions.title: Which minors may be counted, and may women and servants join?
questions.question: The mishnah says that women, slaves and minors do not obligate others in a zimmun. A statement of Rav Assi, cited by Melekhet Shelomoh, says that a baby lying in a cradle is counted. How is this reconciled?

asked_by.name: Melekhet Shelomoh
asked_by.quote: קטן המוטל בעריסה מזמנין עליו והתנן נשים

answers.text: Rambam: the mishnah speaks of a child who does not understand the meaning of the bracha; once he knows to whom we bless, a zimmun is made on him.

sources.name: Rambam
sources.quote: זה שאמר קטנים אין מזמנין עליהם הוא כשלא ידעו ענין

answers.text: Bartenura: only a child who does not know to whom we bless; one who does know is counted, and some say only from age thirteen.

sources.name: Bartenura
sources.quote: דוקא קטנים שאין יודעים למי מברכין, אבל

answers.text: Melekhet Shelomoh: Rav Assi agrees with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, that a baby in a cradle is not counted for a zimmun but may complete the ten.

sources.name: Melekhet Shelomoh
sources.quote: אע"פ שאמרו קטן המוטל בעריסה אין מזמנין עליו אבל עושין אותו סניף

questions.why: It fixes who is a full member of the group.

questions.title: Why does Bartenura rule like the olive-bulk even though Rabbi Yehuda follows it?
questions.question: The preceding mishnah mentioned an olive-bulk without dispute, and here there is a dispute. Why does Bartenura rule that the halakha is like the olive-bulk, and not like Rabbi Yehuda who says an egg-bulk?

asked_by.name: Tosafot Yom Tov
asked_by.ref: Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Berakhot 7:2:3
asked_by.quote: פסק הר"ב וכן הלכה אע"ג דהוי סתם דלעיל

answers.text: Bartenura: the halakha is like the olive-bulk and not like Rabbi Yehuda.

sources.name: Bartenura
sources.quote: כן הלכה, ולא כרבי יהודה

answers.text: Lechem Shamayim: the earlier stam and this dispute do not count as a standing dispute, and in any case the matter is from the Torah, so one follows the stricter view.

sources.name: Lechem Shamayim
sources.quote: אפילו היה מחלוקת שקול. הוי אזלינן

answers.text: Tiferet Yisrael (Boaz): the earlier mishnah only taught that the waiter joins; here we learn that he himself is obligated in the zimmun, so it is not a stam followed by a dispute.

sources.name: Boaz
sources.quote: לפ"ז אפשר לומר דלא הוה סתם ואח"כ

questions.why: It shows how the halakha is decided where a stam mishnah is followed by a dispute.

questions.title: Why is the name of God in Grace after Meals not the same as in the blessing for Torah?
questions.question: In the zimmun of ten we say Elohenu, while in the blessing before the Torah reading we say Hashem. Why were they not given one formula?

asked_by.name: Tosafot Yom Tov
asked_by.ref: Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Berakhot 7:3:2
asked_by.quote: אכתי איכא למידק דלתקנו בתרווייהו בחד נוסחא

asked_by.name: Lechem Shamayim
asked_by.quote: אני תמה ע"ז דאיברא איפכא מסתברא

answers.text: Tosafot Yom Tov: food is given by the attribute of justice, hence Elohim, while the Torah was given only out of kindness.

sources.name: Tosafot Yom Tov
sources.ref: Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Berakhot 7:3:2
sources.quote: אמנם זה מבואר כי המזון הדין נותן לכלכל

answers.text: Hon Ashir: the zimmun was ordained over a cup, and the word cup has the numerical value of Elohim.

sources.name: Hon Ashir
sources.quote: משום דברכת הזמון נתקנה על הכוס, כל

answers.text: Melekhet Shelomoh: at the meal we say Elohut, so that even if we have been satisfied we remember that God's awe rests upon us.

sources.name: Melekhet Shelomoh
sources.quote: גבי ברכת המזון נכון תקנו לומר בשם אלהות כלומר אע"פ

questions.why: It shows how the Rishonim and Acharonim read the choice of divine names in the blessings.

questions.title: Whose opinion is the opening of the mishnah, and where does the dispute begin?
questions.question: The Rashash notes a difficulty: the mishnah says that ten and ten thousand are alike, which seems to conflict with how the Gemara assigns the opening to Rabbi Akiva and the rest to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili. Where does Rabbi Akiva's view end?

answers.text: Rambam: up to 'ten thousand' is Rabbi Akiva, and everything after it is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

sources.name: Rambam
sources.quote: מה שנאמר במשנה הזאת אחד עשרה ואחד עשרה רבוא הוא

answers.text: Bartenura: the opening is Rabbi Akiva, who says there is no difference between many and few once there are ten.

hebrew.summary:
משנה א מונה מי נחשב בשלושה המחייבים זימון: מי שאכל דמאי, מעשר ראשון שנטלה תרומתו, מעשר שני והקדש שנפדו, שמש שאכל כזית, והכותי; אך לא טבל, מעשרות שלא נפדו, שמש שאכל פחות מכזית והנכרי.
משנה ב מוציאה נשים, עבדים וקטנים, וקובעת שיעור כזית, ורבי יהודה אומר כביצה.
משנה ג נותנת את נוסחי הזימון לפי מספר הנוכחים, משלושה ועד רבוא, ואת דברי רבי יוסי הגלילי, רבי עקיבא ורבי ישמעאל.
משנה ד מלמדת ששלושה, ארבעה וחמישה אינם נחלקים, שישה נחלקים, ועשרה אינם נחלקים עד שיהיו עשרים.
משנה ה קובעת ששתי חבורות באותו בית מצטרפות אם רואות זו את זו, ומביאה את מחלוקת רבי אליעזר וחכמים בברכה על יין שלא נמזג.

topics.explanation: זימון הוא ההזמנה שלפני ברכת המזון כששלושה או יותר אכלו יחד. אחד אומר 'נברך' והאחרים עונים. שלושה חייבים בו, ולכן זו חובה ולא מנהג בלבד.

הכותים היו העמים שהביא מלך אשור לערי שומרון. המשנה מונה את הכותי בין המצטרפים לזימון, כי קיבלו את התורה והיו מדקדקים במצוות שקיבלו.
המשנה קובעת שיעור מינימלי לזימון: כזית, ורבי יהודה אומר כביצה. הגמרא לומדת כזית מ'ואכלת'.
